title: 5 Questions to Ask When Selecting Agrochemical Packaging
summary: A packaging system that works well for one crop protection product may not work for another. Chemistry, barrier requirements, closure design, transportation
body_markdown:
A packaging system that works well for one crop protection product may not work for another. Chemistry, barrier requirements, closure design, transportation conditions, regulatory considerations, and sustainability goals can all influence performance throughout a product’s lifecycle.


Before selecting a packaging solution, ask these five questions to help ensure your packaging is aligned with the realities of your application.


## 1. What Does Your Formulation Demand from Its Packaging?


Some solvents may permeate through certain materials over time. Other formulations may interact with packaging components, create internal pressure, or require additional protection to maintain stability during storage and transport. Regulatory and transportation requirements can add further complexity.


That’s why packaging decisions should start with understanding the formulation itself. By identifying your product’s chemical characteristics and performance requirements first, you can better evaluate which packaging solutions are capable of supporting them.


Starting with the container instead of the chemistry can create risks later in the supply chain, including product loss, compromised performance, or packaging failures that could have been avoided during the selection process.


## 2. Does Your Formulation Need Additional Barrier Protection?


For some agrochemical formulations, standard packaging materials provide the protection required. For others, permeation can become a significant concern.


Over time, permeation may contribute to weight loss, odor emissions, or changes in product performance. In these cases, barrier technology becomes an important part of the packaging conversation.


The goal isn’t simply to add a barrier layer. It’s to determine whether additional protection is needed and identify the level of barrier performance that best aligns with the formulation’s requirements.


Making that assessment early can help protect product integrity throughout storage and transportation while supporting operational and regulatory expectations. Greif works with you to evaluate formulation characteristics and match them to appropriate barrier technology options based on application needs.


### 3. What Will Your Packaging Experience After It Leaves the Filling Line?


A package may perform perfectly during filling and still face challenges once it enters the supply chain.


Storage duration, temperature fluctuations, stacking conditions, transportation distances, and repeated handling can all affect packaging performance. The demands placed on a package in a warehouse or transit environment are often very different from those experienced on the filling line.


Evaluating these conditions upfront helps ensure packaging is selected based on the environment it will actually encounter. Otherwise, a packaging system that appears successful during production may struggle when exposed to the realities of distribution and end use.


### 4. Have You Evaluated the Entire Packaging System?


Closures, seals, gaskets, venting systems, and dispensing components all play important roles in package performance. For example, a formulation that creates pressure or vacuum during storage may require a very different closure strategy than one that does not. Similarly, leakage prevention and dispensing performance often depend as much on closure design as container construction.


Looking at individual components in isolation can create blind spots that lead to performance issues later. Evaluating the complete system helps ensure all elements work together to support the specific requirements of the application.


Because packaging performance depends on more than the container alone, Greif and Tri-Sure® work together to help evaluate how every component of the system performs as a whole.


### 5. Can Your Sustainability Goals Work Alongside Performance Requirements?


Sustainability is becoming an increasingly important factor in packaging decisions. Reducing material usage, incorporating recycled content, and advancing circularity goals are all worthwhile objectives. However, for agrochemical applications, sustainability initiatives must be balanced against product protection requirements.


Any packaging change should be evaluated in the context of formulation compatibility, barrier performance, transportation demands, regulatory obligations, and operational needs. The most impactful sustainability decision is not always the one that removes the most material or introduces the highest recycled content.


Instead, it’s the solution that advances environmental goals while continuing to deliver the performance the application requires. Greif can help evaluate packaging alternatives by considering both environmental impacts and performance requirements to identify practical pathways forward.


### The Right Packaging Decision Starts Long Before You Choose a Container


Selecting agrochemical packaging is about more than choosing a bottle, drum, or IBC. It’s about understanding your formulation, identifying potential risks, and evaluating what the complete packaging system must do to protect product performance from filling through end use.


By asking the right questions early, agrochemical manufacturers can make more informed decisions that support product protection, operational efficiency, compliance, and sustainability objectives.
